pr_title: ui: serve ETag header and respect If-None-Match req. header for assets
pr_body:
CockroachDB has included a "Cache-Control: no-cache" response header when serving static, embedded assets for several years now (dating back to as early as 2015), but offered no other way for clients to cache those. Since then, asset sizes have grown considerably larger (currently including ~30MB of JavaScript, a size that will be addressed via other methods) and preventing client-side caching causes noticeable loading delays. Add support for the If-None-Match / ETag pair of request/response headers [1], which allows browsers serve assets from their caches if the cached copy of a requested asset is still the latest copy.

[1] https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/If-None-Match

fixes #62708

issue_context.title: Implement caching for Admin UI JS
issue_context.body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Loading the admin UI is frequently very slow for me. This is because the files are served with no-cache headers, which means that the browser will frequently have to download the entire JS bundle: The connection to the cockroachdb admin from my local machine isn't super fast, however even on fast connections loading 25MB of JS is not going to be speedy. **Describe the solution you'd like** Pass cache-control headers which allow for long lived caching of the file, and cache bust using a query param or new filename when using a new version of cockroachdb. Also, why does the admin panel need 25MB of javascript - from a quick look at the generated bundles it looks like there's a lot of code which may not be needed. **Additional context** We're an enterprise customer. Epic CC-5280 Jira issue: CRDB-2645
